$doc: Canonical package-owned journal structure. Configure a journal directory and IANA timezone in jarvos.config.json or the documented environment variables before creating a journal.

ownership.$doc: journal-lifecycle.js exclusively creates a missing dated file. Obsidian-owned mutation is reserved for authorized active-day backlink and section updates. The derived Journaling.md page has one additive writer; other configured daily-note writers block scheduled creation rather than racing it.

derivedIndex.$doc: The navigation page people actually read. Maintenance adds one embed for a created day in reverse-chronological position, refuses human-authored or actively edited files, and keeps backups outside the synced Journal folder.

required.heading: ## 🚀 Projects
required.description: Ongoing projects from the vault Projects record, as wiki-links. The orientation surface: what you are actually working on, and the shared reference point between you and your assistants. Owned by jarvos-secondbrain-projects.

required.heading: ## 📝 Notes
required.description: Canonical wiki-link hub for notes created or updated that day. Keep salience, memory, and recent-work bullets out of this section.

sections.$optional_doc: Empty by design. Today's Calendar, Apple Reminders, and Paperclip Inbox were removed in favour of a simpler journal — see migration.legacySections. Add new opt-in sections here.

ordering.doc: Sections render in the order listed: all required sections first (in array order), then enabled optional sections (in array order). To reorder, rearrange the arrays above.

structureLock.doc: Structure lock validates that the journal entry matches this config. Required sections must always exist. Optional sections appear only when enabled=true. Unknown sections are flagged (not deleted — content is preserved under the nearest matching section or appended to Notes). Drift is auto-corrected on each heartbeat pass.

migration.$actions_doc: 'rename' folds content into migrateContentTo. 'remove' preserves content as a labelled block under Notes. 'drop' discards the section and its content — use it only for sections whose content was a regenerated daily snapshot, never for anything the user typed.

todays-calendar.heading: ## 📅 Today's Calendar
todays-calendar.doc: Removed to keep the journal focused on what the user writes. Content was a daily snapshot re-fetched from the calendar, so there is nothing to preserve — folding stale event lists into Notes would be noise. Existing journal files are not rewritten in bulk; a file only loses the section if maintenance touches it.

apple-reminders.heading: ## 🔔 Apple Reminders
apple-reminders.doc: Removed for the same reason as Today's Calendar: a regenerated daily snapshot, not authored content. Reminders remain in Apple Reminders, which is their source of truth.

paperclip-inbox.heading: ## 📎 Paperclip Inbox
paperclip-inbox.doc: Removed. Issue-tracker state belongs in the tracker; the journal's job is the human-readable surface. The Projects section is the replacement orientation view.

current-focus.heading: ## 🎯 Current Focus
current-focus.doc: Current Focus was consistently empty and is no longer part of the journal contract. Any legacy content is migrated into Notes.

tasks.heading: ## ✅ Tasks
tasks.doc: Legacy Tasks section is removed. Any existing content is migrated to Notes on first encounter.

notes-created.heading: ## 🗂️ Notes Created
notes-created.doc: Legacy Notes Created content is folded into the canonical ## 📝 Notes section on the next maintenance pass.

extensionGuide.doc: To add a new section: 1) Add an entry to sections.optional with a unique id, heading, source, enabled flag, and description. 2) If the source requires a data-fetch script, add the fetch logic to the heartbeat journal-populate step keyed by the section id. 3) Set enabled=true when ready. 4) Structure lock will automatically include it on the next heartbeat pass. No code changes to heartbeat-procedures.md are needed — it reads this config dynamically.
